LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 8.1.1 STORY TELLING – OGRE NARRATIVE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.1: Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Story telling – Ogre narrative
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Story telling – Ogre narrative, part of Strand 8 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: howcase their traditional attire, ornaments or instruments during the class exhibitions, 1. Why are ogre stories important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to collect a variety of ogre stories from the community and organise in a class portfolio,

2. collaborate with peers to identify features that make a story telling session interesting (e.g. gestures, audience involvement, tonal variation, dramatization),

3. work with peers to draw ogres based on their mental perception,

4. team up to prepare traditional attire, ornaments or instruments that can be used in a storytelling session,

5. showcase their traditional attire, ornaments or instruments during the class exhibitions, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to collect a variety of ogre stories from the community and organise in a class portfolio,
2. collaborate with peers to identify features that make a story telling session interesting (e.g. gestures, audience involvement, tonal variation, dramatization),
3. work with peers to draw ogres based on their mental perception,
4. team up to prepare traditional attire, ornaments or instruments that can be used in a storytelling session,
5. showcase their traditional attire, ornaments or instruments during the class exhibitions, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Story telling – Ogre narrative together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner shows defining personal skills when conducting a story telling session on ogre

stories from African communities.

• Communication and Collaboration: The learner speaks engagingly when discussing moral lessons learnt from the ogre story

and relates them to real life.

Values:
• Unity: This is achieved as the learner works jointly with peers to record the story telling session.

• Responsibility: The learner diligently organises the collection of the ogre stories in the class portfolio.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural Awareness: This is promoted as the learner interacts with ogre stories from various communities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the skill of storytelling to the concept of performance in Creative Arts and Sports.
